reportsMonthly.title: Monthly Engineering Report
reportsMonthly.subtitle: Contribution report for {workspace}, built from synced GitHub activity.
reportsMonthly.noWorkspace: Pick a workspace to report on.

freshness.title: Data freshness
freshness.upToDate: All {count} repositories are synced past the end of {month}.
freshness.stale: {count} of {total} repositories were last synced before {month} ended. Work that landed after their last sync is missing from this report.
freshness.noAdopter: no adopter — nobody's GitHub token is lending this repository a sync
freshness.syncStarted: Sync started for {count} repositories. This can take a few minutes on a first run — regenerate the report when it settles.
freshness.syncNothingToDo: Nothing to sync: no repository has an adopter to sync under.
freshness.syncAdminOnly: Only a workspace admin can start a sync. The report below is built on whatever has synced so far.
freshness.reclaimHint: Reassign an adopter on the repositories page so this one can sync again.

summary.title: Summary
summary.linesHint: lockfiles, build output and generated code excluded
summary.portedHint: same change, more than one branch

members.title: Contribution by member
members.note: Both pull-request columns count what merged this month: "theirs" is what they wrote, "merged by them" is what they pressed merge on — a different job from writing it.
members.caution: Read commit counts with care. Volume reflects branching style as much as output — porting each change onto two branches, or committing from the GitHub web editor, multiplies the count for the same work.

limitations.title: What this report could not measure
limitations.intro: Every figure above rests on synced data. These are the gaps in it.

empty.title: No activity in {month}
empty.body: Nothing landed in this workspace's repositories during this period. If that looks wrong, check the sync state above — a repository that has never synced has no history here yet.

forbidden.title: You do not have access to this report
forbidden.body: The monthly engineering report is available to workspace admins and department heads. It reports on individual contribution, so it is kept to the people who run the team. Ask an admin if you need it.

scope.title: Scope: {departments}.
scope.body: Every figure below counts only the people in your department. Workspace-wide numbers are available to admins.
